segments.text: Have you heard the saying less is more? Well, a new Mayo Clinic study found that may be true when it comes to a certain blood test for adults with type 2 diabetes. Experts say the HBA1C test checks levels of glycated hemoglobin in

your blood and some patients are tested too often. We found that patients who are overtested are more likely to be overtreated despite their baseline good glycemic control. Mayo Clinic Dr. Dr. Rosalina McCoy says unlike home blood

sugar monitoring that patients on insulin do every day, the HBA1C tests blood sugar levels over three months. So patients who are not on insulin and have good blood sugar control only need to be tested once or twice a year instead of
more frequently. This prevents waste, saves time and money, and prevents unnecessary treatments. For more health news, visit the Mayo Clinic News Network. I'm Vivian Williams.
